reason: planning stopped before any code was written: the plan still needed revising in the last round (round 3 of 3). I checked the plan's claims by reading the snapshot. The APIs it names all exist with the expected shapes: resolve_tip/RecordsTip with At{tip, from}, RECORDS_REF and RECORDS_TRACKING_REF, Git::at, discover, run, rev_parse, ls_tree_under and cat_blobs, check_record_file returning Option<AnyRecord>, the WorkItem fields, WorkDecision.work_item, Ladder and may_change, and site::source_url with start 0 meaning no anchor. xtask/Cargo.toml already depends on athena-data and athena-git, so no new dependency is needed. Each demonstration calls a real seam on real fixtures, not a test double. Each would fail without the behavior it covers. Links, refusals, absent fields and page states are well covered. One soundness problem remains. The recommendation rule guesses at the raising role's limit even though that limit can be read cheaply from role records through athena-data. Because athena-core's split_open shows that in-limit proposals are approved without a person, the plan's 'Decide yourself' line can be false for proposals at the design-decisions and defaults-conventions rungs. That makes the derived recommendation wrong on those rungs, so the verdict is revise. Findings: major: The recommendation guesses the role's limit when it could be read, so 'Decide yourself' can be wrong for open proposals that the system approves without a person. (Approach, RECOMMENDATION RULE; Decision 1, third rejected alternative; Open question 5); minor: The stated run command does not run one of the three tests the demonstration relies on. (Demonstration for criterion 8, Run line); nit: The plan never says which GitHub base the records links use. (Step 4, Pin { base, sha }; Step 5)
